episodes.191876: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon on Saturday (7/13) as the area reached its convective temperature.  These initial storms produced large hail up to 3 inches, gusty winds, and heavy rainfall across central Wisconsin.  Flash Flooding was reported in Wausau as 2 to 3 inches of rain fell during the afternoon. ||A line of severe thunderstorms, associated with a mesoscale convective vortex, then tracked through central and east-central Wisconsin during the late afternoon and early evening hours on Saturday (7/13).  These storms produced damaging winds, small hail, and heavy rainfall.  Flash Flooding was noted in the Appleton area as 2.5 to 3.5 inches of rain fell during the early evening hours.
episodes.191914: Scattered clusters of storms resulted in large hail over portions of east-central Minnesota during the afternoon on July 13. One storm produced a brief tornado in Rice County. A line of storms then developed over northwestern Minnesota during the evening and travelled southeast across central Minnesota throughout the night. This line led to numerous reports of hail and wind damage before it weakened as it moved into Wisconsin.||An unusually warm and humid air mass resulted in heat index values greater than 100F across portions of southern and western Minnesota during the afternoon and evening of July 13. The combination of several thunderstorms and persistent cloud cover kept heat index values in the low to mid 80s further east.
episodes.191925: A line of very intense thunderstorms moved from southeast to northwest through the Tucson Metro area. The storm was most intense from midtown Tucson extending to the northwest into portions of Marana. Wind damage was extensive across the much of the Tucson Metro with an estimate of thousands of fallen trees, numerous power poles down, building damage to several buildings, widespread sign damage, roof damage and vehicle damage due to fallen trees. This event also resulted in 1 to 2.5 inches of rain and numerous swift water rescues.
episodes.191945: A very strong mid level ridge slowly moved through the region, resulting in multiple days of excessive heat. At least one instance of injury and fatality were reported from the heat. The strong ridge eventually shifted far enough east and south of the area to allow sufficient moisture to return, resulting in the development of diurnal convection, with some thunderstorms yielding strong wind gusts.
episodes.191975: A line of storms produced high winds and wind damage across a good portion of central South Dakota during the late evening Saturday July 13th into the early morning hours Sunday July 14th. This line of storms produced wind gusts in excess of 60 mph with a peak wind gust of 109 mph 13 miles north northwest of Sansarc, along with sporadic damage prior to reaching the cities of Pierre and Fort Pierre. In and around the Pierre area, there were numerous reports of toppling of trees or limbs coming down in addition to damage to several buildings, outbuildings, campers and signage. The peak wind gust recorded by the weather station at Pierre regional airport was 84 mph. 12 weather stations spread across 10 counties recorded peak winds in excess of 70 mph. Power infrastructure was also impacted by this system with 412 customers reported to have lost power.
episodes.191981: A disturbance generated a round of severe storms across the region during the late afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.192050: Scattered thunderstorms moved across parts of northern Illinois during the afternoon of July 13th producing isolated wind damage.||Scattered thunderstorms developed during the evening of July 13th and continued into the early morning of July 14th producing significant flash flooding in Rockford as well as isolated wind damage.
episodes.192052: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois during the morning of July 14th producing isolated wind damage, heavy rain and isolated flooding.  Numerous locations reported thunderstorm wind gusts between 40 and 50 mph.
episodes.192053: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northwest Indiana during the morning of July 14th producing isolated severe winds.
episodes.192054: A line of thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the late evening of July 13th and the early morning of July 14th.  A second line of thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the mid morning of July 14th.
episodes.192090: Thunderstorms over Orange County produced a severe wind gust and a funnel cloud.
episodes.192145: An extended period of moderate to heavy rainfall moved in with a deep moisture tap surging north around a deep upper level low drifting over Southwest. This moisture surge caused minor flooding on streams in Anchorage as well as widespread flooding of roadways with impacts to transportation.
episodes.192241: Sporadic wind damage was reported among sub-severe wind gust observations.
episodes.192243: A waterspout was reported by Emergency Management.
episodes.192426: An isolated thunderstorm produced a few localized severe downbursts near Annapolis.
episodes.192438: An isolated thunderstorm produced wind gusts to nearly hurricane force over middle portions of the Chesapeake Bay offshore of Annapolis and Kent Island.
episodes.192590: A surface trough oriented from southwest to northeast stretched across the Piedmont and into southeastern Virginia became the focus for widely scattered shower and thunderstorm activity during the afternoon and evening of July 14th. Activity initially developed in southern Virginia in the afternoon and strengthened as it tracked southeastwards into the Albemarle and Pamlico Sounds during the evening hours, with some of these storms becoming strong in nature and producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.192761: Monsoonal moisture coming from the south increased PWAT values and increase instability to produce thunderstorms that caused high wind gusts.
episodes.192780: An upper level disturbance combined with a warm and humid airmass to produce thunderstorms across the Ohio Valley.
episodes.192781: An upper level disturbance combined with a warm and humid airmass to produce thunderstorms across the Ohio Valley.
episodes.192974: Southeast Ohio underwent a heatwave during the middle of July with daily chances of showers and strong thunderstorms each afternoon from the 14th through the 17th. Storms extended down from the Great Lakes region by the peak of the afternoon and brought forth strong enough wind gusts to produce downed trees and power lines. Activity then quickly crossed the Ohio River into West Virginia each evening, bringing the severe weather threat to an end.
episodes.192975: Daily showers and thunderstorms were observed across northeast Kentucky during the middle of July in the midst of unseasonably hot temperatures. Thunderstorm complexes initially developed up near the Great Lakes and would then venture through the Ohio Valley each day and reaching eastern Kentucky by the peak of the afternoon. Damaging winds accompanying these storms resulted in downed trees within Greenup and Lawrence Counties before departing eastward into West Virginia on both July 14th and 16th.
episodes.193030: On the afternoons of July 14th and 16th, eastward progressing thunderstorm complexes ventured into West Virginia and brought strong to severe storms through the state. Downed trees and power lines were most common on both days as damaging wind gusts accompanied the convection. The risk for severe weather remained brief both days as activity quickly pivoted east into Virginia and Maryland by the evening.
episodes.193145: Between 630-830 PM MDT, severe thunderstorm winds moved across Custer County and over the town of Miles City. Wind speeds up to 77 mph were reported resulting in widespread significant tree damage including the uprooting of large trees which in some cases fell on vehicles and other property. Downed power lines caused power outages across the Miles City area. At least one rooftop was reported blown off a house. Power outages and large tree damage was also reported in Fallon County in Baker where the airport recorded a wind gust of 79 mph.  In addition, one location in northwest Custer County recorded 2.92 inches of rainfall in 30 minutes and hail up to nickel size covered the ground.
episodes.193334: Moderate to strong instability combined with sufficient shear and several shortwave troughs created chances for strong to severe storms. Hail, wind gusts, and reported tornadoes occurred.
episodes.193335: Moderate to strong instability combined with sufficient shear and several shortwave troughs created chances for strong to severe storms. Hail, wind gusts, and reported tornadoes occurred.
episodes.193460: Supercell thunderstorms developed over southeast Montana and merged into a line of severe thunderstorms as the moved across far southeast Montana and into northwest South Dakota. The storms produced widespread wind gusts of 50 to over 80 mph, with some areas within the line producing wind gusts of 80 to over 100 mph. Considerable damage was noted with the stronger wind gusts across portions of northwest South Dakota, especially southern Harding, northern Butte, northern and eastern Meade, and Haakon counties.  The line of storms was classified as a derecho event as it tracked more than 250 miles across the region from southeast Montana to central South Dakota.
episodes.193471: A severe thunderstorm developed behind the passing derecho, producing wind gusts to over 60 mph.
episodes.193745: Thunderstorms over central and southern South Dakota, produced strong winds across far northern Nebraska during the early morning hours of July 14th. Measured wind gusts to near 60 MPH were reported in the Valentine and Butte areas.
episodes.193751: An upper level disturbance crossed the region during the 13th helping support the development of afternoon and evening thunderstorms. An isolated thunderstorm reached severe levels in southern Penobscot county producing damaging winds around Glenburn.
episodes.194083: A couple lines of strong to severe thunderstorms moved across southern WI with reports of damaging winds, large hail, and flash flooding. The storms developed along a warm front.
episodes.194183: Thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening hours on July 13th. These initially took on supercell characteristics producing hail both near the Mississippi River and across portions of Dodge County before moving southeast and forming into a line of storms that produced localized wind damage.
episodes.194188: First line of stronger storms to develop during an active couple day period to push out over Lake Michigan.
episodes.194288: Surface heating combined with adequate moisture to produce isolated thunderstorms across northeast Mississippi during the afternoon hours of July 14, 2024. Strong winds damaged a few trees and powerlines across northern Monroe County.
episodes.194403: During the afternoon and evening hours on July 13th, storms of various modes moved across portions of western Wisconsin producing both large hail and damaging wind gusts. As storms progressed eastward, they developed into a line and continued to produce wind damage as they moved into central Wisconsin.
episodes.194472: Isolated thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours along the sea breeze. One of these thunderstorms became strong enough to produce strong wind gusts and large hail in the North Charleston area.
episodes.194557: A shortwave trough tracking across the area caused strong thunderstorms to develop. As the storms crossed the lakes, they caused wind gusts meeting Special Marine Warning criteria. Storms were strongest across the western portion of the area before weakening with eastward progression.
episodes.194558: A shortwave trough tracking across the area caused strong thunderstorms to develop. As the storms crossed the lakes, they caused wind gusts meeting Special Marine Warning criteria. Storms were strongest across the western portion of the area before weakening with eastward progression.
episodes.194610: After midnight on July 14th, a line of thunderstorms moved across portions of western Wisconsin. As these storms moved over already saturated soils from storms a few hours prior, susceptible areas noted flooding and rock slides particularly in Trempealeau and Monroe Counties.
episodes.194620: A stationary front lingered over the area through the day. Some showers and thunderstorms developed as a weak shortwave moved overhead in the afternoon hours with just enough MLCAPE (1000 J/kg) to break a mid-level cap. One storm was able to reach severe limits and produce damaging wind gusts in northeast NJ.
episodes.194643: Severe thunderstorms formed over eastern Montana ahead of an upper level short wave trough and jet streak. Most of the severe weather remained over Montana and South Dakota, but a few storms grazed southwestern North Dakota resulting in severe wind gusts. The strongest reported wind gust of 85 mph occurred to the northeast of Scranton, in Slope County.
episodes.194645: A round of upper level short wave troughs passed from eastern Montana and Saskatchewan into North Dakota during the late afternoon and early evening hours. This led to thunderstorm development in an environment of strong deep layer shear and elevated instability, with multiple supercells occurring. These storms produced very large hail and damaging wind gusts as the storms spread to the southeast. Two storms produced significant damage. The first one produced wind gusts of 80 mph to the northeast of Drake, McHenry County, which combined with ping pong ball size hail to cause extensive damage to crops and property. The second occurred to the south-southeast of Cleveland in which 3.5 inch diameter hail combined with high winds to severely damage two houses and crops in the area.
episodes.194749: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a surface trough produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.194755: Afternoon and evening thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce strong marine wind gusts in the Tampa Bay area.
episodes.194770: At the surface, the Lake Erie region resided within the warm/moist sector, along the northwestern flank of the Bermuda-Azores subtropical high pressure ridge, during the afternoon through early evening of the 14th. Simultaneously, a cold front drifted southeastward across the far-northwestern Great Lakes, Upper Mississippi Valley, and vicinity. Well-ahead of the front, clusters of multicell showers and thunderstorms persisted generally eastward over and near the western-half of Lake Erie and generated a couple of gale-force peak convective wind gusts along the Lorain County shore during the early evening. These storms encountered moderate MUCAPE, DCAPE, and effective bulk shear, respectively.
episodes.194773: Rounds of thunderstorms during the middle of July led to increased runoff across portions of western Wisconsin. As a result, several river basins rose into flood stage with the passage of these storms. Most notably, the Kickapoo River at Ontario entered major flood stage with a river stage of just under 20 feet.
episodes.194961: Monsoon moisture seeping in from the south fueled isolated thunderstorms, a few of which produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.194962: Monsoon moisture seeping in from the south fueled isolated thunderstorms, a few of which produced high winds.
episodes.195024: Thunderstorms occurred during the early morning hours of July 14th. In the East Jordan area, lightning struck a mobile home, setting it ablaze and resulting in a total loss of the structure. All occupants survived, though all were hospitalized for their injuries, including one occupant who was transported to a larger hospital for treatment.
episodes.195046: An organized line of thunderstorms developed across western South Dakota during the evening hours of July 13 and spread eastward through the night. The environment featured 2000-3000 J/kg MUCAPE, 25 to 35 knots of deep-layer shear, and an increasingly warm and dry capped layer farther eastward through South Dakota. Widespread damaging wind developed with the mesoscale convective system with gusts from 60 to 75 mph common.
episodes.195047: An organized line of thunderstorms developed across western South Dakota during the evening hours of July 13 and spread eastward through the night. The environment featured 2000-3000 J/kg MUCAPE, 25 to 35 knots of deep-layer shear, and an increasingly warm and dry capped layer further eastward through South Dakota. Widespread damaging wind developed with the mesoscale convective system with gusts from 60 to 75 mph common. The storms weakened rapidly as they entered northwest Iowa, but still managed to cause some damage just over the border from South Dakota.
episodes.195179: Upper-level flow the evening of the 13th features a low-amplitude shortwave trough that had ejected out into the northern Great Plains. At the surface, a weakening stationary front was noted on WPC surface analysis to extend from northwest Nebraska into southeast Nebraska. Isolated strong thunderstorms that developed along this boundary brought a single severe wind gust in Knox County. However, the primary impact of this episode was the excessive heat that impacted much of southeast Nebraska and southwest Iowa. Heat indices the afternoon of the 15th in this area peaked between 110 and 115 degrees. The highest heat index was 117 degrees, observed by an AWOS station in Harlan, Iowa.
episodes.195184: A shortwave trough moved into a moist and unstable environment, with high DCAPE over the region. Pulse convection developed, with downdrafts downing several trees and power lines across the state.
episodes.195185: A shortwave trough moved into a moist and unstable environment, with high DCAPE over the region. Pulse convection developed, with downdrafts downing several trees and power lines across the state.
episodes.195188: A shortwave trough moved into a moist and unstable environment, with high DCAPE over the region. Pulse convection developed, with downdrafts downing several trees and power lines across the state.
episodes.195221: Increasing moisture across eastern Utah and western Colorado, in association with a weak monsoonal push, brought an increase in shower and thunderstorm coverage. This was the first day of the moisture surge, meaning that surface levels of the atmosphere remained unsaturated, favoring virga and strong, gusty outflow winds.
episodes.195259: Thunderstorms occurred in mid July with monsoonal flow. A few thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall on July 14.
